newsitem.title: SPAIN: Santander buys 51 pct of Brazil's Banco Geral.
newsitem.headline: Santander buys 51 pct of Brazil's Banco Geral.

text.p: Spain's Banco Santander said on Friday it had bought a 51 percent majority share in Brazil's Banco Geral do Comercio.
"Banco Santander will assume the managerial control and take a 51 percent controlling stake in Banco Geral," the bank said in a statement.
The bank said the transaction was subject to final approval by the Brazilian and Spanish authorities.
Santander, Spain's largest bank, said the deal would involve a maximum investment of about $220 million via capital increases, to be paid over a three year period.
Santander said it would value Banco Geral at a maximum of 1.4 times book value for the purposes of its stake in the bank.
Banco Geral has pro-forma consolidated assets of $1.2 billion and a consolidated net worth of $154 million.
Brazilian authorities have approved an expansion of Banco Geral's 77 offices to 200 full branches, which would make it the largest foreign controlled bank in the country in terms of branch network.
